paragraphs.text: But I say that so long as the heir is a child, he differeth nothing from a bondservant though he is lord of all;
paragraphs.original: Λέγω δέ, ἐφʼ ὅσον χρόνον ὁ κληρονόμος νήπιός ἐστιν, οὐδὲν διαφέρει δούλου κύριος πάντων ὤν,
paragraphs.translit: Legō de, ephʼ hoson chronon ho klēronomos nēpios estin, ouden diapherei doulou kyrios pantōn ōn,

paragraphs.text: but is under guardians and stewards until the day appointed of the father.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ ἐπιτρόπους ἐστὶ καὶ οἰκονόμους ἄχρι τῆς προθεσμίας τοῦ πατρός.
paragraphs.translit: alla hypo epitropous esti kai oikonomous achri tēs prothesmias tou patros.

paragraphs.text: So we also, when we were children, were held in bondage under the rudiments of the world:
paragraphs.original: οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς, ὅτε ἦμεν νήπιοι, ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου ἤμεθα δεδουλωμένοι·
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai hēmeis, hote ēmen nēpioi, hypo ta stoicheia tou kosmou ēmetha dedoulōmenoi·

paragraphs.text: but when the fulness of the time came, God sent forth his Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
paragraphs.original: ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ χρόνου, ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ, γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός, γενόμενον ὑπὸ νόμον,
paragraphs.translit: hote de ēlthen to plērōma tou chronou, exapesteilen ho theos ton hyion autou, genomenon ek gynaikos, genomenon hypo nomon,

paragraphs.text: that he might redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.
paragraphs.original: ἵνα τοὺς ὑπὸ νόμον ἐξαγοράσῃ, ἵνα τὴν υἱοθεσίαν ἀπολάβωμεν.
paragraphs.translit: hina tous hypo nomon exagorasē, hina tēn hyiothesian apolabōmen.

paragraphs.text: And because ye are sons, God sent forth the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba, Father.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι δέ ἐστε υἱοί, ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς καρδίας ἡμῶν, κρᾶζον· Αββα ὁ πατήρ.
paragraphs.translit: hoti de este hyioi, exapesteilen ho theos to pneuma tou hyiou autou eis tas kardias hēmōn, krazon· Abba ho patēr.

paragraphs.text: So that thou art no longer a bondservant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir through God.
paragraphs.original: ὥστε οὐκέτι εἶ δοῦλος ἀλλὰ υἱός· εἰ δὲ υἱός, καὶ κληρονόμος διὰ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hōste ouketi ei doulos alla hyios· ei de hyios, kai klēronomos dia theou.

paragraphs.text: Howbeit at that time, not knowing God, ye were in bondage to them that by nature are no gods:
paragraphs.original: Ἀλλὰ τότε μὲν οὐκ εἰδότες θεὸν ἐδουλεύσατε τοῖς φύσει μὴ οὖσι θεοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: Alla tote men ouk eidotes theon edouleusate tois physei mē ousi theois·

paragraphs.text: but now that ye have come to know God, or rather to be known by God, how turn ye back again to the weak and beggarly rudiments, whereunto ye desire to be in bondage over again?
paragraphs.original: νῦν δὲ γνόντες θεόν, μᾶλλον δὲ γνωσθέντες ὑπὸ θεοῦ, πῶς ἐπιστρέφετε πάλιν ἐπὶ τὰ ἀσθενῆ καὶ πτωχὰ στοιχεῖα, οἷς πάλιν ἄνωθεν δουλεύειν θέλετε;
paragraphs.translit: nyn de gnontes theon, mallon de gnōsthentes hypo theou, pōs epistrephete palin epi ta asthenē kai ptōcha stoicheia, hois palin anōthen douleuein thelete;

paragraphs.text: Ye observe days, and months, and seasons, and years.
paragraphs.original: ἡμέρας παρατηρεῖσθε καὶ μῆνας καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἐνιαυτούς.
paragraphs.translit: hēmeras paratēreisthe kai mēnas kai kairous kai eniautous.

paragraphs.text: I am afraid of you, lest by any means I have bestowed labor upon you in vain.
paragraphs.original: φοβοῦμαι ὑμᾶς μή πως εἰκῇ κεκοπίακα εἰς ὑμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: phoboumai hymas mē pōs eikē kekopiaka eis hymas.

paragraphs.text: I beseech you, brethren, become as I [am], for I also [am become] as ye [are]. Ye did me no wrong:
paragraphs.original: Γίνεσθε ὡς ἐγώ, ὅτι κἀγὼ ὡς ὑμεῖς, ἀδελφοί, δέομαι ὑμῶν. οὐδέν με ἠδικήσατε·
paragraphs.translit: Ginesthe hōs egō, hoti kagō hōs hymeis, adelphoi, deomai hymōn. ouden me ēdikēsate·

paragraphs.text: but ye know that because of an infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel unto you the first time:
paragraphs.original: οἴδατε δὲ ὅτι διʼ ἀσθένειαν τῆς σαρκὸς εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν τὸ πρότερον,
paragraphs.translit: oidate de hoti diʼ astheneian tēs sarkos euēngelisamēn hymin to proteron,

paragraphs.text: and that which was a temptation to you in my flesh ye despised not, nor rejected; but ye received me as an angel of God, [even] as Christ Jesus.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὸν πειρασμὸν ὑμῶν ἐν τῇ σαρκί μου οὐκ ἐξουθενήσατε οὐδὲ ἐξεπτύσατε, ἀλλὰ ὡς ἄγγελον θεοῦ ἐδέξασθέ με, ὡς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ton peirasmon hymōn en tē sarki mou ouk exouthenēsate oude exeptysate, alla hōs angelon theou edexasthe me, hōs Christon Iēsoun.

paragraphs.text: Where then is that gratulation of yourselves? for I bear you witness, that, if possible, ye would have plucked out your eyes and given them to me.
paragraphs.original: ποῦ οὖν ὁ μακαρισμὸς ὑμῶν; μαρτυρῶ γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι εἰ δυνατὸν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὑμῶν ἐξορύξαντες ἐδώκατέ μοι.
paragraphs.translit: pou oun ho makarismos hymōn; martyrō gar hymin hoti ei dynaton tous ophthalmous hymōn exoryxantes edōkate moi.

paragraphs.text: So then am I become your enemy, by telling you the truth?
paragraphs.original: ὥστε ἐχθρὸς ὑμῶν γέγονα ἀληθεύων ὑμῖν;
paragraphs.translit: hōste echthros hymōn gegona alētheuōn hymin;

paragraphs.text: They zealously seek you in no good way; nay, they desire to shut you out, that ye may seek them.
paragraphs.original: ζηλοῦσιν ὑμᾶς οὐ καλῶς, ἀλλὰ ἐκκλεῖσαι ὑμᾶς θέλουσιν, ἵνα αὐτοὺς ζηλοῦτε.
paragraphs.translit: zēlousin hymas ou kalōs, alla ekkleisai hymas thelousin, hina autous zēloute.

paragraphs.text: But it is good to be zealously sought in a good matter at all times, and not only when I am present with you.
paragraphs.original: καλὸν δὲ ζηλοῦσθαι ἐν καλῷ πάντοτε, καὶ μὴ μόνον ἐν τῷ παρεῖναί με πρὸς ὑμᾶς,
paragraphs.translit: kalon de zēlousthai en kalō pantote, kai mē monon en tō pareinai me pros hymas,

paragraphs.text: My little children, of whom I am again in travail until Christ be formed in you--
paragraphs.original: τέκνα μου, οὓς πάλιν ὠδίνω μέχρις οὗ μορφωθῇ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν·
paragraphs.translit: tekna mou, hous palin ōdinō mechris hou morphōthē Christos en hymin·

paragraphs.text: but I could wish to be present with you now, and to change my tone; for I am perplexed about you.
paragraphs.original: ἤθελον δὲ παρεῖναι πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἄρτι, καὶ ἀλλάξαι τὴν φωνήν μου, ὅτι ἀποροῦμαι ἐν ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: ēthelon de pareinai pros hymas arti, kai allaxai tēn phōnēn mou, hoti aporoumai en hymin.

paragraphs.text: Tell me, ye that desire to be under the law, do ye not hear the law?
paragraphs.original: Λέγετέ μοι, οἱ ὑπὸ νόμον θέλοντες εἶναι, τὸν νόμον οὐκ ἀκούετε;
paragraphs.translit: Legete moi, hoi hypo nomon thelontes einai, ton nomon ouk akouete;

paragraphs.text: For it is written, that Abraham had two sons, one by the handmaid, and one by the freewoman.
paragraphs.original: γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Ἀβραὰμ δύο υἱοὺς ἔσχεν, ἕνα ἐκ τῆς παιδίσκης καὶ ἕνα ἐκ τῆς ἐλευθέρας·
paragraphs.translit: gegraptai gar hoti Abraam dyo hyious eschen, hena ek tēs paidiskēs kai hena ek tēs eleutheras·

paragraphs.text: Howbeit the [son] by the handmaid is born after the flesh; but the [son] by the freewoman [is born] through promise.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ ὁ μὲν ἐκ τῆς παιδίσκης κατὰ σάρκα γεγέννηται, ὁ δὲ ἐκ τῆς ἐλευθέρας διʼ ἐπαγγελίας.
paragraphs.translit: allʼ ho men ek tēs paidiskēs kata sarka gegennētai, ho de ek tēs eleutheras diʼ epangelias.

paragraphs.text: Which things contain an allegory: for these [women] are two covenants; one from mount Sinai, bearing children unto bondage, which is Hagar.
paragraphs.original: ἅτινά ἐστιν ἀλληγορούμενα· αὗται γάρ εἰσιν δύο διαθῆκαι, μία μὲν ἀπὸ ὄρους Σινᾶ, εἰς δουλείαν γεννῶσα, ἥτις ἐστὶν Ἁγάρ,
paragraphs.translit: hatina estin allēgoroumena· hautai gar eisin dyo diathēkai, mia men apo orous Sina, eis douleian gennōsa, hētis estin Hagar,

paragraphs.text: Now this Hagar is mount Sinai in Arabia and answereth to the Jerusalem that now is: for she is in bondage with her children.
paragraphs.original: τὸ δὲ Ἁγὰρ Σινᾶ ὄρος ἐστὶν ἐν τῇ Ἀραβίᾳ, συστοιχεῖ δὲ τῇ νῦν Ἰερουσαλήμ, δουλεύει γὰρ μετὰ τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς·
paragraphs.translit: to de Hagar Sina oros estin en tē Arabia, systoichei de tē nyn Ierousalēm, douleuei gar meta tōn teknōn autēs·

paragraphs.text: But the Jerusalem that is above is free, which is our mother.
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ ἄνω Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐλευθέρα ἐστίν, ἥτις ἐστὶν μήτηρ ἡμῶν·
paragraphs.translit: hē de anō Ierousalēm eleuthera estin, hētis estin mētēr hēmōn·

paragraphs.text: For it is written, Rejoice, thou barren that bearest not; Break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: For more are the children of the desolate than of her that hath       the husband.
paragraphs.original: γέγραπται γάρ· Εὐφράνθητι, στεῖρα ἡ οὐ τίκτουσα, ῥῆξον καὶ βόησον, ἡ οὐκ ὠδίνουσα· ὅτι πολλὰ τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐρήμου μᾶλλον ἢ τῆς ἐχούσης τὸν ἄνδρα.
paragraphs.translit: gegraptai gar· Euphranthēti, steira hē ou tiktousa, rhēxon kai boēson, hē ouk ōdinousa· hoti polla ta tekna tēs erēmou mallon ē tēs echousēs ton andra.

paragraphs.text: Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are children of promise.
paragraphs.original: ὑμεῖς δέ, ἀδελφοί, κατὰ Ἰσαὰκ ἐπαγγελίας τέκνα ἐστέ·
paragraphs.translit: hymeis de, adelphoi, kata Isaak epangelias tekna este·

paragraphs.text: But as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him [that was born] after the Spirit, so also it is now.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ ὥσπερ τότε ὁ κατὰ σάρκα γεννηθεὶς ἐδίωκε τὸν κατὰ πνεῦμα, οὕτως καὶ νῦν.
paragraphs.translit: allʼ hōsper tote ho kata sarka gennētheis ediōke ton kata pneuma, houtōs kai nyn.

paragraphs.text: Howbeit what saith the scripture? Cast out the handmaid and her son: for the son of the handmaid shall not inherit with the son of the freewoman.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ τί λέγει ἡ γραφή; Ἔκβαλε τὴν παιδίσκην καὶ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτῆς, οὐ γὰρ μὴ κληρονομήσει ὁ υἱὸς τῆς παιδίσκης μετὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἐλευθέρας.
paragraphs.translit: alla ti legei hē graphē; Ekbale tēn paidiskēn kai ton hyion autēs, ou gar mē klēronomēsei ho hyios tēs paidiskēs meta tou hyiou tēs eleutheras.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore, brethren, we are not children of a handmaid, but of the freewoman.
paragraphs.original: διό, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἐσμὲν παιδίσκης τέκνα ἀλλὰ τῆς ἐλευθέρας.
paragraphs.translit: dio, adelphoi, ouk esmen paidiskēs tekna alla tēs eleutheras.
